problem.text: Sidorenko's conjecture beyond graphs built recursively from trees and norming graphs.

claims.text: Theorem 1.1: if binom(|A|, r) binom(r, k) divides the number of degree-k vertices of B for each k, then H is Sidorenko; Theorem 1.2: if B is r-regular and |B| >= binom(|A|, r), then H is Sidorenko; Corollary 1.3: every bipartite graph has a one-sided blow-up (p = |A|! suffices) that is Sidorenko; the square of K_{5,5} minus C_10 is Sidorenko.

assumptions.text: Weakly norming reflection hypergraphs (Conlon-Lee 2017) and the Conlon-Fox-Sudakov theorem.

methods.text: The Holder trick averaging over relabellings of A, reducing to downset and incidence graphs that are weakly norming.

evidence.text: Complete proofs; an earlier version's error was corrected, giving the divisibility condition.

limitations.text: The degree-count conditions require many vertices of each degree; graphs with few vertices on the regular side, such as the 2026 counterexample (22 faces against binom(13, 3) = 286) or the Heawood graph (7 against binom(7, 3) = 35), are not covered.

relevance.text: The one-side-regular criterion is the closest positive theorem to incidence graphs of 3-uniform hypergraphs; it marks what the girth-six and sphere candidates must go beyond, and K_{5,5} minus C_10 is again named as the simplest open case.
